ORRIN MARINE RESEARCH UNIT. Technical Report TR-2026-07 (Final, revision 2). Title: Artificial settlement tiles and juvenile
mussel recruitment at Calder Sound.
Executive summary. Between March 2025 and April 2026 the Unit deployed 36 monitoring stations along the northern shore of
Calder Sound to test whether textured concrete tiles raise settlement of juvenile blue mussels (Mytilus spat). Monitoring ran for 14
months. Three treatments were compared: untreated rock (control, Group A), ribbed tiles (Group B) and smooth tiles (Group C).
Ribbed tiles raised mean settlement by 84% relative to control; smooth tiles raised it by 22%. The work was funded by the Calder
Coastal Trust under grant CCT-5521 for a total of GBP 148,000.
Abbreviations: ORU, Orrin Marine Research Unit; SD, standard deviation; n, number of quadrat counts.

3. Results. Table 1 gives mean settlement by treatment across all valid monthly counts (spat per 100 cm2).
Group A (control) | n=48 | mean 3.2 | sd 0.7
Group B (ribbed) | n=48 | mean 5.9 | sd 1.1
Group C (smooth) | n=45 | mean 3.9 | sd 0.9
The difference between B and A was significant (p < 0.001). The difference between C and A was smaller and reached p = 0.03. B

were cracked, and a fourth was found displaced in the February 2026 survey.
